subject.title: [BUG] OpenAI Codex errors leak into user chat

question: For unconfigured Codex/OpenAI failures that reach chat delivery, should OpenClaw silently suppress them, show a safe generic provider-unavailable message, or only normalize the raw `detail` payload?
rationale: The source-backed parser gap is narrow, but the issue's expected behavior asks for a delivery policy that affects provider routing, channel replies, and user visibility.

options.title: Safe generic error plus parser fix
options.body: Recognize `detail` payloads and replace unconfigured-provider leaks with generic, non-raw user copy while keeping actionable configured-provider errors visible.

options.title: Silent suppression
options.body: Discard errors proven to come from providers the user did not configure, which reduces noise but may hide setup or runtime drift.

options.title: Parser-only fix
options.body: Only normalize FastAPI-style `detail` payloads and defer provider-discovery gating to a separate issue or PR.

recommendation.title: Safe generic error plus parser fix
recommendation.body: Recognize `detail` payloads and replace unconfigured-provider leaks with generic, non-raw user copy while keeping actionable configured-provider errors visible.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this person to both shared AI runtime changes and Codex/OpenAI provider direction, which are the decision surfaces here.
